Issue to fix: Problem: I am using Pandas to get a dataframe like this: name a b c 0 Aaron 3 5 7 1 Aaron 3 6 9 2 Aaron 3 6 10 3 Brave 4 6 0 4 Brave 3 6 1 5 David 5 1 4 I want to replace each a with a unique ID so output looks like: name a b c 0 Aaron 1 5 7 1 Aaron 1 6 9 2 Aaron 1 6 10 3 Brave 2 6 0 4 Brave 1 6 1 5 David 3 1 4 How can I do that? Thanks! A: import pandas as pd df = pd.DataFrame({'name': ['Aaron', 'Aaron', 'Aaron', 'Brave', 'Brave', 'David'], 'a': [3, 3, 3, 4, 3, 5], 'b': [5, 6, 6, 6, 6, 1], 'c': [7, 9, 10, 0, 1, 4]}) result = ... # put solution in this variable BEGIN SOLUTION Notes from similar past work are below. They may or may not apply to this problem; use them only if they help. Way: Replace values in pandas DataFrame columns that occur less than a specified frequency threshold with a placeholder value. 1. Calculate the frequency of each unique value within the target column. [uses: pandas.Series.value_counts] 2. Identify the index of values whose counts fall below the required minimum threshold. 3. Replace the identified rare values with a designated placeholder string. [uses: pandas.Series.replace] 4. Apply the replacement logic across multiple columns of the DataFrame. [uses: pandas.DataFrame.apply] Pitfalls: - Ensure the threshold is applied per column rather than across the entire DataFrame if columns have different distributions. - Verify that the placeholder value (e.g., 'other') does not conflict with existing data that should be preserved. - Confirm that the replacement logic handles columns where all values meet the threshold without introducing NaNs. Verified solution of that past problem: ```python def replace_rare_values(col): counts = col.value_counts() # Identify values that appear fewer than 2 times mask = counts < 2 # Get the list of values to be replaced to_replace = counts[mask].index # Replace those values with 'other' return col.replace(to_replace, 'other') result = df.apply(replace_rare_values) ``` Similar solved problems (NOT verified to apply; adapt them): 1. Rest of the rows from the dataframe should not change. Output A B 0 AB 1 1 CD 4 2 EF 3 3 GH 5 The order of the rows of df must not change i.e. CD should remain in index 1. I tried using outer merge which is handling index but duplicating columns instead of overwriting. >>> pd.merge(c,d, how='outer', on='A') A B_x B_y 0 AB 1.0 NaN 1 CD 2.0 4.0 2 EF 3.0 NaN 3 GH NaN 5.0 Basically B_y should have replaced values in B_x(only where values occur). I am using Python3.7. A: import pandas as pd C = pd.DataFrame({"A": ["AB", "CD", "EF"], "B": [1, 2, 3]}) D = pd.DataFrame({"A": ["CD", "GH"], "B": [4, 5]}) result = ... # put solution in this variable BEGIN SOLUTION Its verified solution: ```python result = pd.concat([C, D]).drop_duplicates(subset='A', keep='last').sort_values('A').reset_index(drop=True) ``` Begin.
